transcript.content: Hello, welcome. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I can’t seem to slow down. Lately it feels like I’m just always going—finish something at school or at home, and then I’m immediately onto the next thing. Like I can’t really shut myself off.
Have you noticed that you need less sleep lately, or that you feel rested even if you haven’t slept much?
Not really. I mean, I sleep… about the same, I think. I don’t wake up feeling especially rested or anything like that.
Have you found yourself talking more than usual or feeling like you can’t stop talking, even if others might not want to listen?

Yeah… I guess so. In meetings or parent conferences, I’ll mean to just say something quick, and then I’m still talking—giving examples, telling some classroom story, throwing out ideas they didn’t ask for. I can usually tell they’re trying to wrap it up, but it’s hard to stop.
Have you noticed your thoughts racing or jumping from one idea to another lately, like your mind is going too fast to keep up with?
I’m not sure. I mean, I get distracted, but I wouldn’t say my thoughts are racing exactly. It’s more just… hard to pin down, I guess.
Have you been starting or doing a lot more things lately—like taking on new projects, making a lot of plans, or feeling driven to keep going even if you're tired?

Yeah… I think that’s part of why I’m here. I don’t know if it’s “projects” exactly, but I’m just… always moving. I finish one thing at school or at home and then I’m right into the next thing. It feels like I can’t really shut it off.
Have you felt unusually good, maybe even overly confident or on top of the world lately?
Not really. I mean… I don’t think I’ve felt on top of the world or anything like that. Maybe just busy, but not unusually good.
Have you found yourself doing things without thinking them through, or taking risks you normally wouldn’t, like spending more money, driving faster, or making big decisions quickly?
I don’t think so. I mean, I might act a little quick sometimes, but not like… big risks or spending a bunch of money or anything. Nothing that really stands out.
Have you been feeling more irritable or emotionally up and down lately—like small things are getting under your skin more than usual?
I don’t know… not more than usual, I guess. I mean, little things bother me sometimes, sure, but I haven’t really noticed a big change.
Have you noticed that you feel physically restless lately—like you can’t sit still, need to move around, or are pacing more than usual?

Yeah… I guess that’s actually a big part of why I’m here. I just feel like I’m always going, like I finish something at school or at home and then I’m immediately onto the next thing. I don’t really feel like I can shut it off.
Has this restlessness or constant need to keep moving and doing things caused you any problems at work, at home, or with other people?

Yeah… it has. At work it’s gotten bad enough that they put me on a corrective plan, which is… hard to say out loud.

And at home, my spouse says the routines—caregiving stuff—are harder because everyone’s kind of managing my energy too. I’m trying to help, but it feels like I’m wearing people down, and maybe damaging trust with them.
How often do you feel this constant need to keep moving and doing things—almost every day, or does it come and go more randomly?
Almost every day, I’d say. It’s not really random. I feel like I’m just… running on a motor most of the time, like I finish one thing and I’m already onto the next. Hard to shut it off.
Do you notice that this constant need to keep moving and doing things is worse at certain times of the day, like in the morning or at night, or does it feel about the same all day long?

It’s… kind of all day, I think. I don’t notice one time being clearly worse. It’s more like once I’m moving, I just keep going—school, home, whatever—and I jump right into the next thing without really shutting off.
Have you had any distinct periods of time—maybe a few days or more—where you felt different from your usual self, almost like a shift in your mood, not just being busy or restless?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed a clear shift like that. It feels more like I’m just like this most of the time, not a separate few days where I’m suddenly different.
Have you had any periods where you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy, even if it was just for a few days?
Not really… I mean, everyone has off days, but I can’t think of a period where I felt hopeless or stopped caring about things like that.
Have you had any distinct periods of time—maybe four days or more—where you felt unusually high, elated, or irritable, not just being busy or restless?
No… I don’t think so. I can get irritated, sure, but not like a separate stretch of days where I felt unusually high or different.
Have you ever had a period where you felt a sudden surge of energy, like you didn’t need sleep or felt on top of the world, even for just a few days?
No… not really. I can get wound up or stay busy, but I don’t think I’ve had that “on top of the world” feeling or not needing sleep for days.

Have you ever had a time when your mood or energy was so high that other people noticed a clear change in you—like you were unusually excited, overly confident, or needed much less sleep for several days in a row?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, people might notice I’m restless sometimes, but not like… a clear change where I’m overly confident or not sleeping for days.
Have you ever had a time when you felt a sudden surge of energy, like you didn’t need sleep or felt on top of the world, even for just a few days?
Not that I can think of. I’ve had times I’m keyed up, but not like I didn’t need sleep or felt… unusually great for days.
Have you ever had a time when your energy or mood was so high that it was clearly different from your usual self, even for just a few days in a row?
I don’t think so. I mean… I have my usual ups and downs, but nothing that stands out as clearly different for several days.

inference_history.note: Initial presentation of persistent overactivity and inability to slow down raises possibilities of manic/hypomanic episodes (F30.1, F31.1), ADHD (F90.0), adjustment disorder with anxiety (F43.0), or even early signs of a depressive episode with agitation (F32.0). Further questioning is needed to clarify mood symptoms, sleep patterns, duration, and potential stressors.
